While promoting the upcoming season premiere of “Law and Order,” the show’s Instagram page posted a photo of Hargitay and Brunson on set and shared the following caption: “Two iconic New York Captains walk onto a set… 📸
Hargitay has spoken about her admiration of Brunson on several occasions, referring to him as a “friend” and calling him “my inspiration” in June while appearing on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle.
“He is so singular and magnificent. He’s a magnificent human,” she said.

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Episode 9 Recap: Death By Poisoned Chalice
summary: Read a recap of “The Traitors: New Blood” Episode 9 to find out who survived the Highland Feast and how many Traitors are still in the turret as the end of the game approaches.
story: Warning: Spoilers from “The Traitors: New Blood” Episode 9 below.
One Faithful has spent their last night in the castle after unknowingly drinking from a poisoned chalice, eliminating them from the game.

In Episode 9 of “The Traitors: New Blood,” which aired Nov. 5, the remaining players put on their fanciest clothes to attend Alan Cumming’s Highland Feast, a celebration after successfully banishing their first Traitor of the season.

But the party wasn’t just an opportunity for the players to bond. Prior to the gathering, the Traitors were secretly informed that they had to poison a Faithful’s chalice and murder them. With the Traitors down a member, they needed to remove the correct player from the game in order to regain the upper hand and paint a target on a Faithful.
Read on to find out who survived the Highland Feast and how many Traitors are still in the turret as the end of the game approaches.
The Highland Feast Brings Tears and Chaos

Episode 9, titled “Playing Chess,” opens with the players gathering around a table for a seemingly more pleasant evening. Some of the players become emotional as they share what the game has meant to them. Ben says he finally feels like “one of the boys” after forming strong connections with the men and Abbey B. reveals she is grateful for the experience because her home life has been “isolating” while she cares for her daughter. Shane also opens up about the death of his sister and how it has impacted his family.

Alan interrupts the heartfelt conversation as the episode rewinds to two hours earlier. Traitors Katie and Joe are shown entering the confessional room where they receive a note that reads, “Traitors, tonight after the dinner someone will be poisoned. Whilst everyone is getting ready for dinner, you must sneak down and meet in the secret room to decide who you want to murder by assigning that player a poisoned chalice.”

But there was an additional twist. “Each player must drink, however, they do not have to drink their own glass,” the message said. “They can discuss and drink someone else’s glass instead. If a Traitor ends up drinking from the poisoned chalice, there will be no murder tonight.”

Katie and Joe begin to strategize. He worries he is in a “dead man walking situation” following Tomica’s banishment and Victor publicly declaring that he would target Joe next. Joe says he needs “to do something drastic” to save himself and suggests poisoning Victor. But Katie reminds him that Victor might switch his drink with someone else and disrupt their plans.

Back at the Highland Feast, the players join Alan outside and he reveals one of them will be murdered after drinking from a poisoned glass. He tells them they have two minutes until he makes his toast — whichever glass they are holding when he begins his speech will be the one they drink from.

Victor is immediately anxious and wants a player to switch drinks with him. He asks Joe, who declines. Kriste is also disinterested in changing her glass which makes Ben suspicious. Before time runs out, Shane and Joe swap drinks. In his confessional, Joe confirms that the Traitors pulled off the murder. “Today, we’re back in the win column,” he says.
A Murder and a Spirited Challenge With a Hidden Shield

At breakfast, multiple players start sharing their theories. Abbey B. questions why Joe didn’t want to switch with Victor while Jay says he still suspects Victor is a Traitor. Shane is suspicious of Joe, as well, but Ben is focused on Katie and Kriste.

The players arrive in groups until it is revealed that Morgan was murdered. “They gave me the poisoned chalice!” Morgan says when she learns she was killed. After reading the note from the Traitors, she tells the camera, “And that kids is why you do not drink something you didn’t pour yourself at parties.”
She continues, “Shoot! This was the hardest thing I’ve ever done. But also the coolest thing. I wouldn’t change anything other than swap my glass. That’s for sure.”
The Faithfuls are confused by Morgan’s murder. They briefly discuss her departure before Alan strolls into the Breakfast Room and tells them, “Keep your spirits up.”

The players meet Alan at his creepy cabin in the woods. For the mission, they have to enter the shack and summon a spirit. The spirit will call them and name an item they want to be reunited with. The players must find the correct item and hand it over. If they answer correctly, they will receive $9,000 per item. If they are wrong, the player who delivers the item will be dragged from the cabin. There is also a shield up for grabs.

The players work together to give the spirit the right bottle of beer in round one. But during round two, they fail to find the exact wedding dress and Jay is eliminated. In between rounds, Victor finds a shield and quickly stows it away without anyone seeing. For the final round, Abbey B. braves a smelly bathroom to grab the last item, adding $18,000 in total to the prize pot.
The Traitors Prepare to Battle

Going into the Round Table, Katie says she is aware Joe’s name is being thrown out. But, she wants to try to save him and keep the Traitors in power. During the day, she mentioned Wyatt and Kriste to other players, hoping to point them in the wrong direction.

However, her tactic did not work on Victor. He says in his confessional that he is certain Joe is a Traitor and he will work hard at the Round Table to get everyone on his side. He says he will not back down and will try to stop the players from voting for Kriste.
Joe is also ready to fight for survival. “It’s me versus Victor, and I’m going to come out on top,” he says as the episode ends.
What Will Happen Next Week?

Episode 10, “The Sun, the Moon and the Truth,” will show Victor and Joe going head-to-head at the Round Table. If Joe survives, the Traitors will have a better chance of winning the game. But if he is banished, Katie will be left alone in the turret.
The next episode will be released on Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8 p.m. PT/ET and 7 p.m. CT on NBC. The episode will also stream the next day on Peacock.
In just two weeks, the season will conclude in an epic two-hour finale on Thursday, Nov. 19.

title: Aaron Carter’s Ex Shares Update on Their Son on Anniversary of His Death
summary: The late Aaron Carter’s ex, Melanie Martin, shared a heartfelt tribute, including an update on their son Prince, on the four-year anniversary of the singer’s death.
story: It’s been four year since Aaron Carter died, and his fiancée is honoring her late love, while also sharing an update on their son, Princeton Lyrik Carter.
In an Instagram post shared Nov. 5, Melanie Martin first reflected on the day that forever changed her life.

“Some days it feels like yesterday, and other days it feels like a lifetime ago. I still wish I could hear your voice, tell you about our day, or have just one more conversation with you,” she wrote, adding that she missed the man she know “behind closed doors.”
“You were so much more than the headlines or the struggles people saw. I wish the world had shown you more kindness and compassion,” she added.
Amid her grief, she shared some insight on now-4-year-old Princeton.
“The hardest part is watching Prince grow up without you,” Martin wrote. “He’s learning so much and becoming his own little person.”
She added that she wishes the “I Want Candy” singer “could see every milestone. I promise he will always know how much his daddy was loved.”
She continued to share how Carter’s death taught her the importance of mental health and the need to get proper care.

“You never know what someone is silently fighting,” she wrote, later adding, “Grief doesn’t have an expiration date. I can smile, make memories, and keep going for our son while still missing you every day. Both things can be true.”
She concluded by reminding people to check on their loved ones and be gentle with those who are struggling.
“A little compassion can mean more than you realize. I wish our story had a different ending,” she wrote. “I wish you had more time. Forever in my heart, Aaron.”

Martin has shared photos and videos of Prince over the years. Most recently she posted their Harley Quinn and Joker Halloween costumes. The young boy was seen sporting his late dad’s signature haircut from when he was a rising star.
Carter’s twin sister Angel Carter Conrad also shared a tribute on her Instagram story, expressing how much she misses him.
“I love that you still find ways to visit me in my dreams, especially during life’s biggest moments,” she wrote, adding how she will also continue to honor his memory.
Carter was found dead in his Lancaster, California, home on Nov. 5, 2022, at the age of 34. He had struggled with addiction and mental health issues over his lifetime.

The teen idol died by accidental drowning in his bathtub after inhaling difluoroethane and taking alprazolam, the generic form of Xanax, according to a Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner-Coroner report.

title: Lauren Speed-Hamilton to Host a New YouTube Series, ‘Pull Up.’ See the Trailer
summary: Reality television star Lauren Speed-Hamilton is prepared to push her guests outside of their comfort zones in her new celebrity interview series. Watch the exclusive trailer.
story: Reality television star Lauren Speed-Hamilton is prepared to push her guests outside of their comfort zones in her new celebrity interview series.
TODAY.com can exclusively reveal that the “Love Is Blind” alum, who found love on Season 1 of the Netflix dating show, will host “Pull Up,” premiering on YouTube Thursday, Nov. 12.

For the first season, Speed-Hamilton, will be joined by “The Real Housewives of Atlanta” star Cynthia Bailey, comedian KevOnStage, husband Cameron Hamilton and more guests for candid conversations in unexpected places. Speed-Hamilton will stop by the recording studio to chat with some guests, put her strength to the test in an aerial class with another and challenge her husband to an axe throwing contest when they meet up.
In a trailer for the series, exclusively shared by TODAY.com, Speed-Hamilton introduces the show by asking, “Who wants beef? I’m ready.”
Later when she interviews her husband, she jokes, “Is Cam trying to leave me on this show?”
After revealing the other three guests who will appear in Season 1, she says, “Crazy, right? But we’re going to get into it all.”
See the full trailer below.
Prior to the trailer release, Speed-Hamilton teased the new project on her Instagram story Nov. 4. She shared with fans that she is the creator and executive producer of “Pull Up.”

“This show has been such a labor of love,” she said. “First off, what possessed me to create a huge project like this in my first year of motherhood? I don’t know. But we did it y’all. And it turned out so amazing, so great, and I’m so proud of it. I’m really excited for y’all to see it.”

“Pull Up” will be available to watch on the couple’s “Hanging With The Hamiltons” YouTube channel. The two previously had a podcast they released on their channel called “The Love Seat” where they spoke about love and relationships, including with fellow “Love Is Blind” stars Brett and Tiffany Brown and Amber Pike and Matt Barnett.
Recently they have been posting videos about entering a new chapter as first-time parents after welcoming their son, Ezra William Hamilton, in October 2025.
They shared a joint post on Instagram Nov. 1 celebrating Ezra’s first year. In the adorable clip, Speed-Hamilton cradled her newborn and said, “I’m your mommy.”
The clip showed the parents bonding with their baby boy and sharing sweet moments with him every month of the past year as Ezra learned to take his first steps.

title: Al Roker Inducts Scarlett Johansson into Very Special ‘5-Timer’s Club’
summary: Scarlett Johansson has hosted TODAY weather with Al Roker five times which means he is in the five timer’s club.
story: If the whole acting thing doesn’t work out for Scarlett Johansson, she can always fall back on another one of her skills: forecasting the weather.

While stopping by Studio 1A to discuss her new film “Paper Tiger,” the star marked a special milestone with TODAY’s resident weatherman, Al Roker, and helped him share the forecast for the fifth time live on TODAY.
“This is your fifth time. So much like they do on ‘SNL,’ we got you your fifth weather robe,” Al said as he helped the star put the robe on.
“Five-timers club!” Savannah said.

On “Saturday Night Live,” celebrities who host the show five times are typically presented with a special velvet jacket with the number five on it. Johansson is one of many stars who have received the honor.
The actor was touched by the gesture and hugged Al, saying, “This is a dream.”
“And we even have a little thunderbolt on the back for you,” Al pointed out.
“How chic,” the star said. “Oh my God, can I wear this out? It’s like a little dinner robe.”
As she approached the weather map, Johansson was impressed by how much activity was going on across the country.
“My gosh, you guys, look at all this. It looks like there’s a bunch of rain happening over here here along the coast,” she said.
As she examined the map, the actor pointed out one state that’s currently having gorgeous weather.
“Florida is where you want to be right now. That looks nice and roasty toasty,” she said.
As she made her way to the west coast, Johansson was surprised to see weather in the 30s in the Western Plains.
“What’s that all about?” she asked Al.
“It’s about fall,” he quipped.
Al and Johansson then highlighted some more rain on the east coast and the weatherman acknowledged that it’s been pretty dry lately.
“We’re so happy that there’s rain out there,” the actor said.
And just like that, the segment was over, and Al took a moment to congratulate the star.
“This was the best fifth weather ever!” he said.
“Yay!” Johansson exclaimed as she raised her arms in the air.

title: Met Gala Announces New 2027 Theme After Original Exhibit Was Canceled Amid Controversy
summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art has announced its new theme for the 2027 Met Gala after scrapping its originally planned exhibition around British designer John Galliano.
story: The Metropolitan Museum of Art has announced its new theme for the 2027 Met Gala after scrapping its originally planned exhibition around British designer John Galliano.

The new theme for the gala and the Costume Institute’s spring exhibit revolves around jeans and T-shirts and is called “extraORDINARY: Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday,” according to a Nov. 5 news release.

The exhibit will be “devoted to the undersung beauty and allure of quotidian garments—think the aforementioned t-shirts and jeans, plus raincoats, sweatshirts, puffer jackets, and more,” according to an announcement from Vogue.
The gala will explore how designers have reinvented everyday wear for the runway and used materials like paper, aluminum and plastic, “inviting visitors to see them anew.”
The 2027 Met Gala is being organized by curator in charge Andrew Bolton, who previously said he supported the decision not to go forward with the Galliano theme.

“It was really important to come up with an exhibition that wasn’t just a masterwork show or something that we could do a little bit more easily,” Bolton told Vogue. “That was really important to me: to come up with an idea that wasn’t a substitute. And it had to have some sort of contemporary resonance.”
The new theme comes just over two months after the Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that it was abandoning its planned theme around Galliano’s work, titled “John Galliano: Horizons.”

The theme faced a wave of criticism related to anti-Semitic and racist comments Galliano made in 2010 and 2011, some of which were captured on video. He was castigated for making comments about Jewish and Asian people on two separate occasions at the same Paris bar. He was fired as Dior’s creative director in the aftermath of the comments.
He said in court his remarks were made due to drug and alcohol addiction. Galliano has said that he is now sober.
Bolton issued a statement after the Met Gala scrapped the idea of a Galliano-themed event.
“I believe deeply in the responsibility of museums to examine difficult histories with rigor, candor, and care,” Bolton said.

“I also recognize the pain and concern this exhibition has caused,” he added. “After extensive discussion, I support the decision not to proceed. I remain deeply grateful to my colleagues and to the advisors, lenders, collaborators, and community leaders who contributed their knowledge, trust, and perspectives to the project.”

title: Al Roker Preps for His Memorable ‘Seinfeld’ Cameo in 1993
summary: See Al Roker prepare for his cameo on “Seinfeld” in 1993.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Al Roker on Dec. 5, 1993, preparing for his classic cameo on “Seinfeld.”
Al Roker is synonymous with TODAY, but he also lent his talents to another NBC series during its heyday.
Yes, Al famously appeared as himself on an episode of “Seinfeld” that aired during the sitcom’s fifth season on Dec. 9, 1993.
A few days before that, though, on Dec. 5, Al took TODAY viewers behind the scenes for his cameo.
What Advice Did Al Get From ‘Seinfeld’ Star Jerry Seinfeld?
“It’s my big break, my acting debut, a shot at stardom,” Al joked in a voiceover as he walked onto the “Seinfeld” set.
Al then chatted up the cast to get some tips on how he should approach his role.
“It’s really just pretending,” “Seinfeld” star and creator Jerry Seinfeld told him.
Jason Alexander Shared a Different Perspective
Co-star Jason Alexander had a more dire take on the matter.

“One thought that should be going through your head at all times is, ‘Please, God, don’t let me screw it up,’” he said matter of factly. “If you take all the acting training that I’ve had and you distill it down to that, that’s basically what I do.”

Alexander took it a step further by also encouraging Al to play “who passed wind” if the camera lingers on him when the scene ends. He showed what that kind of facial expression looks like and how effective it can be.
“It’s good for any situation. It covers everything,” he said.
Did Al Win Over the ‘Seinfeld’ Cast?

In the episode, Al, appearing on the cover of TV Guide, becomes a key cog in the plot. The segment captured Al rehearsing his big scene, which took place on a New York City subway. Co-star Julia Louis-Dreyfus was not impressed when he later asked her if he had potential.
“No, I don’t, Al,” she quipped. “You’re talentless, Al.”
Al was surprised to learn the cast doesn’t get nervous, but he powered through, regardless, and got a nice round of applause from the audience when Seinfeld introduced him after the shoot.

title: Parents, sister of far-right Kraków shooter found dead in family home
summary: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in the Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.
story: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in the Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.

Investigators are looking at the deaths of the shooter’s parents and sister as they unravel events surrounding the random violence in the Polish city’s historic center, Main Market Square, around 3 p.m. on Saturday.
The relatives, who lived about 90 miles from Krakow, likely died from gunshot wounds, according to police.
Authorities said the shooter, who survived a shootout with police and remains in the hospital, wore a bulletproof vest during the attack.

The identifications were made as world leaders paid tribute to victims and Poland declared two national days of mourning after a shooter motivated by far-right ideologies killed six people in Kraków on Saturday, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.”

Victims of the attack included a man from the United Kingdom, a woman from Austria and four Polish nationals, according to regional official Krzysztof Jan Klęczar. The injured included visitors from Britain, Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria, according to the Associated Press.
St. Mary’s Basilica in the square paused its hourly trumpet call overnight in honor of the victims. It was the first time the historic church had done so since World War II.

The gunman, described by officials as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs, is reported to have opened fire in Kraków’s main market square. Four women and two men were killed in the midday attack, the country’s deadliest shooting in decades, while a policeman who confronted the gunman is in critical condition.

The suspect is being investigated on suspicion of murder in connection with the six deaths, Polish Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said on X Sunday, adding that he “acted with the aim of seriously intimidating a large number of people, making this a terrorist offence.”

The same suspect is facing a separate murder charge over killings in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie, Żurek said, a town some 93 miles northeast of Kraków where three of the man’s relatives were found dead in his home.

“Establishing all the circumstances of these tragic events, determining the full sequence of the perpetrator’s actions and securing evidence are currently the priorities of the investigation,” which is being led by terror offense specialists within the prosecutor’s office, he said.
Krakow‘s prosecutor Eryk Stasielak said the shooter was in critical condition and victim autopsies were set to start on Monday, according to PAP, a Polish news service.
“Tomorrow we will be deciding the fate of the attacker, if he survives, because he remains in critical condition,” Stasielak said, according to a translation of the report.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński did not name the suspect but identified him as a Polish national in his mid-20s from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie. He used an automatic rifle, Kierwiński said Saturday, describing him as having “ultranationalistic” views.
“Everything indicates he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” he said.
The suspect was shot by police at the scene and taken to the hospital around 3 p.m. local time. He remains in critical condition, regional governor Krzysztof Klęczar told a news conference Sunday.
A man and two women later found dead in an apartment are believed to be the suspect’s parents and sister, according to Andrzej Fijołek, deputy inspector of Police National Headquarters.
Two national days of mourning on November 8 and 9 were announced by the Interior Ministry on Sunday.

Pope Leo XIV issued a message to the archbishop of Krakow on Sunday expressing sadness over the tragedy. The Pope “implores the gift of Christian hope for the families overwhelmed by grief and joins with all those experiencing these days of mourning,” the message read, according to a translation.
Żurek, the justice minister, said on social media early on Sunday that Senior Constable Jakub Kulik “is fighting for his life in hospital” after he confronted the shooter.
“One of his lungs is not functioning, and he needs every drop of blood he can get,” he posted on X.
Police later said that blood banks in Kraków were full and thanked those who donated.
“Senior constable Jakub Kulik and senior constable Artur Moranski are true heroes,” said Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said, referring to both policemen.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Klęczar said that without “the efficient and selfless intervention” of the officers, “the number of victims could have been significantly higher.”
“The condition of the two police officers remains serious,” Klęczar said Sunday, though Kierwiński later said the two men had been brought out of comas.

Video posted on social media shows what appears to be an injured police officer firing at the gunman before dropping to his knees and rolling over onto his back. The officer, who did not appear to have backup nearby, is seen struggling to reload his firearm and appeared to be clutching his right arm.

Four of the dead in the city center attack have been identified, though their names have not been released. They include four Polish nationals, a British national, and one non-Polish woman whose nationality has not yet been publicized, Klęczar said.
All those wounded were alive on Sunday, he said, adding that 11 of the 16 injured people are Polish and two of the individuals are police officers.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the U.K. government “deeply mourns the British national and other victims” who died in the shooting.
“The U.K. stands resolutely in solidarity with the people of Poland,” he said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also said Saturday that his country “stands in solidarity” with neighboring Poland, calling the shooting a “shocking crime.”
The U.S. State Department said it was not aware of any American citizens harmed in the violence.
“The profound depth of Poland’s shock at the horror of yesterday’s appalling mass murder in Krakow is truly remarkable to behold,” U.S. Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose said in a post on X.

Noting how rare the incident was in a “extraordinarily safe” country like Poland, he added: “There’s something profoundly precious about being in a country where such evil remains so foreign to everyday life, where an entire nation recoils in horror at the mere thought of it, and where the depth of grief reveals the true goodness of its people.”
Part of Main Market Square in Kraków and surrounding streets reopened Sunday, but cordons remain in place while police carry out forensic work, the city has said in a statement.
Several makeshift memorials with flowers and candles appeared across the city on Sunday.
Tourists caught up in attack
Many of those caught up in the attack were tourists visiting the city.

Taylor Dorfmeister, a 21-year-old American student studying in Italy who was visiting Poland, was in the square with his roommate when gunfire erupted. Dorfmeister said there was a delay before the crowd reacted and then everyone began to flee the area. He said he took shelter in a building.
“We ran up the stairs in the building to hide and it was a dead end, which is when I was the most terrified since the gunshots were [loud] and near,” Dorfmeister told NBC News.

It sounded to Dorfmeister like the gunfire was coming from the first floor of the building where he hid. The student from Santa Cruz, California, was “fully prepared for the worst” based on the proximity of the noise, he said.
“This is it,” Dorfmeister thought. “Like, there’s nowhere to go, nowhere to hide.”
Marie-Ange Collaer was visiting with her family from Brussels.

“We literally ran for our lives and managed to hide from the bullets flying around,” she wrote on Facebook. “Lying on the floor in a shop like in a bad police movie whilst you hear bullets everywhere.”
Collaer said her family was shaky and “quite in shock” after returning to their hotel but everyone was grateful to be alive.
“We saw a few that did not make it, true horror,” she wrote.
U.K. resident Neil Thaxton and his wife, Nicky, also survived the attack.

“We had just walked through the main square and heard the gunshots,” Thaxton wrote on Facebook. “We thought it was fireworks then people started running, we went into a gift shop and the staff took us in the back of the shop and locked the doors and turned the lights off.”

title: Gunman kills 6 in ‘terror attack’ in Poland, officials say; 3 others found dead in his home
summary: A gunman described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs fatally shot six people while driving through a public square Saturday in Krakow, Poland, officials said, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.” Three of his relatives were later found dead in his home.
story: A gunman described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs fatally shot six people while driving through a public square Saturday in Kraków, Poland, officials said, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.” Three of his relatives were later found dead in his home.

The relatives were found after the shooter opened fire in Kraków’s Main Market Square, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said. Four women and two men were killed in the midday attack in the city’s popular commerce and tourist destination, police said.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński identified the shooter as a man in his mid-20s from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie, a city some 93 miles northeast of Kraków. He used an automatic rifle, Kierwiński said, describing him as having “ultranationalistic” views.
“Everything indicates he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” he said.
The shooter’s relatives, a man and two women found in an apartment, are believed to be his parents and sister, according to Andrzej Fijołek, deputy inspector of Police National Headquarters.
“We have the next acts of this tragedy,” Tusk said, describing the discovery of the bodies.
The discovery added another layer to the investigation into the attack at the square, which also left at least 15 people injured.
Two police officers were seriously wounded in the shooting, officials said. Tusk named the officers and described them as acting selflessly as the sound of gunfire sent market crowds running.

“Senior constable Jakub Kulik and senior constable Artur Moranski are true heroes,” the prime minister said. “They likely saved lots of lives while risking their own lives. Their conditions are serious but they are in good hands. All of Poland has their fingers crossed for you.”
One of the officers was was described earlier as undergoing surgery. He was shot three times, according to an earlier statement from Kierwiński.

The attacker, a Polish national, was shot by police at the scene and taken to the hospital around 3 p.m. local time. The shots were fired from a vehicle moving through the area, Kraków officials said in a series of posts on X.

An earlier post from the city’s official municipal government account said that investigators were working to determine the scale of the incident. The city announced a mourning period in recognition of the tragedy through Nov. 11.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Four of the dead in the city center attack have been identified, though their names were not released, Polish authorities said. They include three Polish nationals and a foreigner from the U.K., Kraków police and the U.K. Foreign Secretary said.
An Interior ⁠Ministry spokesperson said foreign nationals from Austria, ‌Germany, Portugal, ‌Russia and Britain are among the injured.⁠
The U.S. State Department said it was not aware of any American citizens harmed in the violence.

Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Kraków police, told TVN24 that the gunman was wearing military-style fatigues and used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car.

Video posted on social media shows what appears to be an injured police officer firing at the gunman before dropping to his knees and rolling over onto his back. The officer, who did not appear to have backup nearby, is seen struggling to reload his firearm and appeared to be clutching his right arm.

It was unclear whether the officer seen in the video is the same one mentioned in the interior minister’s update. Małopolska Police wrote in an X post that no officer had been killed, citing what they said were incorrect reports.
Other chilling video clips taken from the scene show a black car racing through the square. Dozens of people begin running in various directions at the sound of gunfire.

Police exchanged gunfire with the attacker as he went on a “wild ride” through the square, which is why victims were found in various locations, police officials said. The shooter continued to fire at officers after he was struck, but he was ultimately subdued, they said.
Some social media clips show responders attempting lifesaving measures on victims. Lifeless bodies could be seen scattered around the streets after the attack.

Taylor Dorfmeister, a 21-year-old American student studying in Italy who was visiting Poland, was in the square with his roommate when gunfire erupted. Dorfmeister said there was a delay before the crowd reacted and then everyone began to flee the area. He said he took shelter in a building.
“We ran up the stairs in the building to hide and it was a dead end, which is when I was the most terrified since the gunshots were [loud] and near,” Dorfmeister told NBC News.

It sounded to Dorfmeister like the gunfire was coming from the first floor of the building where he hid. The student from Santa Cruz, California, was “fully prepared for the worst” based on the proximity of the noise, he said.
“This is it,” Dorfmeister thought. “Like, there’s nowhere to go, nowhere to hide.”

“We are just learning details of the horrific mass shooting in Kraków, a savage and murderous attack that’s shattered the peace of Poland,” Tom Rose, the U.S. ambassador to Poland, wrote on X. “America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Kraków.”

The Main Market Square sits at the heart of Kraków’s medieval Old Town, where centuries of trade transpired under changing political and religious influences. Laid out in 1257, the sprawling plaza is home to the historic Cloth Hall and St. Mary’s Basilica.
It is considered the largest market square in Europe with history preserved in historical homes, houses of worship and ornate palaces, according to the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.
Mansions throughout the square were home to Polish royalty and aristocrats. It was renamed for Adolf Hitler and served as a Nazi propaganda base during the World War II occupation of Poland.

title: Pope Leo, who had cancer surgery weeks ago, begins South American tour
summary: Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.
story: ABOARD THE PAPAL FLIGHT — Three countries in 12 days, a dozen flights, two helicopter rides and nine Masses on a trip covering around 19,000 miles. Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.
The 71-year-old’s long trip across the strongly Catholic region will take him to Uruguay and Argentina, as well as to Peru, where he lived for decades and served as a bishop until 2023.

Leo considers the tour, one of the most grueling undertaken by a Catholic leader in decades, a “homecoming to places where he spent a long time and to which he feels closely connected,” Vatican spokesperson Matteo Bruni told journalists at a briefing Tuesday.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The Chicago-born pontiff, who is also a citizen of Peru, told pilgrims at his weekly audience in St. Peter’s Square on Wednesday that he was ⁠hoping to “strengthen the faith, renew hope” and “rekindle the fire of charity.”
Leo will hold several meetings with survivors of sexual abuse by ​Catholic clergy during the trip, the Vatican has said, without yet providing further details.

Bruni said the pope would also address a range of issues facing the continent, including environmental destruction, ⁠arms trafficking and regional political instability, bringing “a message of communion and unity.”

title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
summary: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown.
story: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown resulting from Democratic midterm victories against the sector’s long-term growth potential.
The tech-focused Nasdaq 100 closed up 1.1% after plunging 6.3% on Thursday, its worst single-day performance since the Covid-19 pandemic.
The broader S&P 500 finished 0.3% higher, after tanking 4.4% Thursday, a drop that wiped out $2.8 trillion worth of wealth on paper.

A strong October jobs report Friday morning increased the odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next policy meeting in December. The prospect of higher borrowing costs helped to push stocks down from their highs earlier in the day.

Investors continue to digest the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections, in which a crop of Democratic candidates were elected to office who had pledged to rein in AI and data centers. They include Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa of Texas, a state that is among the largest data center markets in the country.
The AI boom is responsible for an ever-increasing share of U.S. stock market gains and economic growth, so any threat to the narrative of demand-fueled growth can rattle investors.
“Markets are being punished according to their dependence on the U.S. AI infrastructure cycle,” Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Singapore-based SAXO Markets, told NBC News.
The incoming Democratic-controlled Congress could also tighten scrutiny of the AI industry, including its infrastructure projects, which could cause delays and additional costs.
This would add to existing worries investors already have about the long-term profitability of these investments.
Some analysts viewed Thursday’s dramatic sell-off as overblown —  merely a sign of some froth coming off an overstretched market —  rather than the end of the line for the AI investment boom.
Recent declines are “just speed bumps,” said economist and investor Ed Yardeni.
Rather than spelling doom for the sector, Yardeni said, losses like this week’s could ultimately help keep the AI bubble from overheating.
Until it becomes clearer how much data center construction is truly threatened by newly elected lawmakers, volatility is likely to continue.

“This is a stock market that is trying to figure out the right valuations for the AI trade, which is grappling with a swift sentiment shift after the midterm elections,” said Alex Guiliano, the chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Resonate Wealth Partners.

title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
summary: No explosives have been found, and it isn’t clear who or what is behind the calls, but the threats alone have caused chaos in the skies and airports.
story: LONDON — A wave of bomb threats against passenger airliners caused chaos in the skies and airports of Europe on Thursday, the latest of such incidents this week that have prompted emergency landings and security sweeps on runways.

No explosives have so far been found, and it is not clear who or what is behind the security threats made against at least 14 airliners. But the threats have caused disruption to Europe’s airspace and some of its busiest airports.

The threats against two flights that landed in Rome came by email that cited opposition to “your feminist regime,” the airport confirmed to NBC News. Italy’s prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, is a woman who has conservative views.

One of the first reports involved Aer Lingus Flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome, which changed course near Paris and diverted to a French air force base, the airline said. There, all 151 passengers and six crewmembers were evacuated while a bomb squad inspected the aircraft, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu’s office said in a statement.
Confirmed flights threatened Thursday

Aer Lingus EI402 from Dublin to Rome — received bomb threat over France, made emergency landing at air base and inspected by bomb squad, according to airline and French officials.Finnair AY1761 from Helsinki, Finland, to Rome Fiumicino — escorted into Rome by Italian air force jets, bomb squad search found no explosives, airline said.Finnair AY1471 from Helsinki to Vienna — also received bomb threat, likewise no explosives found, according to airline.LOT Polish Airlines LO235 from Warsaw, Poland, to Brussels — crew made midair checks after receiving threat, "additional screening" once in Brussels found no "suspicious items," airline said.LOT Polish Airlines LO331 from Warsaw to Paris — stopped while taxiing and directed to parking stand where searched, airline said. Passengers continued on trips after switching planes.Ryanair FR3606 from Copenhagen, Denmark, to Sofia, Bulgaria, and Ryanair FR6410 from Madrid to Sofia — both landed normally following bomb threat, no explosives found, according to Bulgarian Transport Ministry.Ryanair FR1730 from London Stansted to Sofia — also received a bomb threat and diverted to Plovdiv, Bulgaria, the Bulgarian Transport Ministry said.Wizz Air WMT3064 from Milan to Bucharest — airport said it was notified of the bomb threat as flight was arriving, bomb squad found nothing.Czech police say four unidentified flights headed for Prague also received threats.
Aer Lingus EI402 from Dublin to Rome — received bomb threat over France, made emergency landing at air base and inspected by bomb squad, according to airline and French officials.
Finnair AY1761 from Helsinki, Finland, to Rome Fiumicino — escorted into Rome by Italian air force jets, bomb squad search found no explosives, airline said.
Finnair AY1471 from Helsinki to Vienna — also received bomb threat, likewise no explosives found, according to airline.
LOT Polish Airlines LO235 from Warsaw, Poland, to Brussels — crew made midair checks after receiving threat, "additional screening" once in Brussels found no "suspicious items," airline said.
LOT Polish Airlines LO331 from Warsaw to Paris — stopped while taxiing and directed to parking stand where searched, airline said. Passengers continued on trips after switching planes.

Ryanair FR3606 from Copenhagen, Denmark, to Sofia, Bulgaria, and Ryanair FR6410 from Madrid to Sofia — both landed normally following bomb threat, no explosives found, according to Bulgarian Transport Ministry.
Ryanair FR1730 from London Stansted to Sofia — also received a bomb threat and diverted to Plovdiv, Bulgaria, the Bulgarian Transport Ministry said.
Wizz Air WMT3064 from Milan to Bucharest — airport said it was notified of the bomb threat as flight was arriving, bomb squad found nothing.
Czech police say four unidentified flights headed for Prague also received threats.
From there, reports of threats in the skies over Europe arrived at a dizzying pace, triggering searches by cabin crews and then again by airport security crews on the ground.
Security operations were launched at airports in Prague; Copenhagen, Denmark; and Warsaw, Poland, where passengers saw the military and police sniffer dogs patrolling the tarmac.

“It is too early to draw conclusions on whether the reported incidents are linked,” Apostolos Tzitzikostas, the European commissioner for sustainable transport and tourism, said at a news conference in Brussels.
British Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander appealed for calm, telling Sky News, “We have established processes for dealing with hoax and malicious threats, and that’s what these threats have been.”

Italian air force jets escorted a Finnair flight from Helsinki to Rome’s Fiumicino Airport “following anonymous reports of a suspected bomb threat,” said a spokesperson for the city’s airport authority. Bomb disposal experts found nothing.

title: Clashes erupt in France as ‘Black Thursday’ protests sweep the nation
summary: “Everything is going up except wages and pensions,” the country’s main unions said. “Anger is immense.”
story: PARIS — Riot police clashed with protesters in Lyon on Thursday as a nationwide public sector strike tapped into growing anger over deteriorating services and the rising cost of living.
Paris’ iconic Eiffel Tower was closed because of the strike.

Officers clad in black helmets and protective clothing charged at crowds in Lyon after the demonstrations against rising living costs and in support of the high school protest movement turned violent and fires were set in the streets. Water cannons were also deployed. Some of the protesters wore gas masks and safety glasses as a precaution against tear gas.
Images from Paris showed students and other protesters facing off against riot police.
Police were “keeping the situation under control, but it remains tense,” the French Interior Ministry said in a statement at 1 p.m. local time (7 a.m. ET).

“Several violent acts have been committed as part of the high school student movement,” the statement said. After fireworks were fired at a school near the southern city of Toulouse, a fire broke out “that burned the student services office,” it added.

In the city of Rennes in northwest France, metal pétanque balls were thrown at officers, the statement said, adding that police had been pelted with other projectiles in the cities of Pau and Orléans.

title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
summary: Six women alleged that the British comedian had sexually assaulted them at his home, in hotels and public bathrooms. Brand has denied all claims.
story: LONDON — British comedian and actor Russell Brand was found guilty of rape and sexual assault in a London court Thursday.

Brand, ⁠once ‌one of Britain’s highest-profile ‌broadcasters and the ‌former husband of ⁠singer Katy Perry, had denied the accusations, saying the incidents ‌had ​been ‌consensual, reinvented ⁠or reimagined.

Brand, 51, was accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault. Ultimately, he was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He ⁠was acquitted of ⁠the other charges.
He had pleaded not guilty to all counts and consistently denied all of the allegations.

The judge, Justice Joel Bennathan, told Brand in court that the consequence of the verdicts is a “significant custodial term” and that he would have to remain in prison until he is formally sentenced Monday.
“You’ve been convicted of a number of offenses, including rape,” Bennathan said, adding that Brand inevitably faced a “significant” prison sentence.
The maximum sentence for rape is life imprisonment, and it is 10 years for one count of sexual assault, according to Britain’s Sentencing Council.
An investigation into allegations of rape made by two women continues, a spokesperson for London’s Metropolitan Police said.

The accusations date to Brand’s rise as a stand-up comedian and risqué presenter on British television. He also had a prominent radio show on the BBC and wrote several bestselling autobiographies in which he detailed his addictions to drugs and alcohol.
At the height of his fame, Brand featured in several Hollywood movies, including “Forgetting Sarah Marshall” and “Get Him to the Greek.”
His fame stateside was cemented when he briefly wed Perry in a lavish ceremony in India in 2010. The couple divorced in 2012.

title: Melania Trump calls for ‘enduring’ Russia-Ukraine peace as she hosts top officials at the White House
summary: Ukraine has been reeling from the worst collapse in relations with Washington since the start of the war.
story: First lady Melania Trump expressed hope that a humanitarian ceasefire around a city in Ukraine would inspire progress toward a “more enduring” peace, as she hosted representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday.

The unprecedented meeting came as the Trump administration pushes for progress in broader peace negotiations, with the United States set to lead renewed trilateral talks with Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates next week.

Speaking at the White House, the first lady expressed hope that the six-day ceasefire around Oleshky would inspire a peace “more enduring than a temporary ceasefire,” before praising the “highly cooperative” Russian and Ukrainian leaders for helping bring about the pause.

Melania Trump was joined by Kirill Dmitriev, Vladimir Putin’s special envoy, who thanked her on behalf of the Russian leader. “This humanitarian mission shows what can be achieved when compassion, determination and cooperation come together,” he said.
Russia has repeatedly rejected calls for a wider ceasefire since launching its full-scale invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.

The limited ceasefire around Oleshky, which started Oct. 27 and lasted six days, allowed for the evacuation of hundreds of people trapped by fighting, blockades and extensive minefields, via neighboring Belarus. The city in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region was home to 2,000 remaining residents on the brink of starvation.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Both sides held fire throughout the truce, making it the largest de-escalation effort since the war began.

Urging the first lady to keep going with her mission, David Arakhamia, the head of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s ruling faction in Ukraine’s parliament, said he hoped the deal would create momentum “to actually keep the peace when the peace comes.”
Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian parliamentary commissioner for human rights, then presented Melania Trump with Ukraine’s highest state honor, the Order of Princess Olga, 1st Class.
Melania Trump then gave Dmitriev and Arakhamia personal letters to deliver to Putin and Zelenskyy.
She did not respond to shouted questions from NBC News.

title: U.S. Marine dies in Japan during training, military says
summary: The person, who has yet to be named, died Tuesday in Okinawa, the 3rd Marine Division said.
story: A U.S. Marine has died in Japan following a “training incident,” the military said in a statement Wednesday.

The unnamed Marine was undertaking training at Camp Schwab in Okinawa, Japan’s southernmost prefecture, the statement said. The area is home to a large U.S. military presence and bases that serve as a regional hub in the Indo-Pacific.

The Marine, who was with the 3rd Marine Division, died Tuesday and will not be named until 24 hours after the individual’s family has been notified, the 3rd Marine Division said in a statement Wednesday.
For Subscribers
“It is with heavy hearts that 3rd Marine Division announces the death of a Marine following a training incident at Camp Schwab, Okinawa, Japan, on Nov. 3, 2026,” the statement said.
“The circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation,” it added. “We express our deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of our Marine.”
For Subscribers

Okinawa was under U.S. occupation following World War II until it was handed back to Japan in 1972. Today, the U.S. population on the island is nearly 80,000, with nearly 30,000 being active-duty troops from all four branches of the armed forces, though the Marines make up the bulk of the forces.

Separately, Secretary of State Marco Rubio last month pledged to cooperate with Japanese authorities investigating allegations that a ​U.S. Marine murdered a woman in Okinawa. The case sparked widespread protests and led to a U.S. military curfew and mandatory training in standards and discipline.
Lt. Gen. Benjamin Watson, commander of the III Marine Expeditionary Force, said at the time that serving on the Japanese island “comes with responsibility.”

title: U.S. will stop $4B in aid to Israel at the end of the year, Trump says
summary: Oil prices slid in response to the deal, which the president said was Netanyahu’s idea.
story: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that he has made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the U.S. to stop sending $4 billion in aid annually to Israel.
It was not immediately clear which exact funding Trump meant.
Trump said that he and Netanyahu “made a deal months ago that we’re stopping” and that the money would get “cut off at the end of the year.”

Trump said in a phone interview with “Fox & Friends” that the idea was Netanyahu’s — Netanyahu has previously floated tapering American aid over the next decade. Netanyahu’s office declined to comment Tuesday.

“We’ll help Israel if they need it — you know they’ve been a great ally,” Trump said, adding that the Israeli government was “fine with it, because, you know, they have become a very successful country” and “they don’t need” the money.

Trump was speaking while voters were heading to the polls for the midterm elections. U.S. military aid to Israel and Israel’s use of American weapons in Gaza and the West Bank have been among the most contentious issues during the campaign.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Trump appeared to acknowledge a political dimension to the decision, saying, “The left uses the $4 billion payment that everybody knows about, when it’s no secret, as a signal of unfairness, and we can’t allow that to happen.”
“I don’t like that, because, you know, it’s too easy. It’s almost too easy a target,” he said.

“Why should we suffer the slings from lunatics like an El-Sayed when they don’t need it?” Trump added, referring to Abdul El-Sayed, the progressive Democratic Michigan Senate nominee, who has forcefully criticized Israel and U.S. foreign policy during the campaign.

The price of Brent crude oil slid 3%, to $101 a barrel, in response to Trump’s comments, its lowest in more than three weeks, as investors and traders viewed the comments as possibly further evidence that the Iran war could be ended without escalation. It ticked back up to $103 at noon ET.
The initial drop added to oil’s biggest one-day decline in three months Monday, after Trump told NBC News that he was not planning to attack Iran after the midterms.
Complex aid picture

The U.S. has agreed to give Israel $3.8 billion annually as part of a “memorandum of understanding” signed in 2016 during the Obama administration. The agreement, which took effect in October 2018, specifies $3.3 billion a year in military financing grants and $500 million a year for joint missile defense. It is due to expire in 2028.
Almost all of that money must be spent on purchases from the U.S.
But the total amount is much higher, with American military aid to Israel greatly boosted following the Hamas-led attack on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, and the subsequent Israeli assault on Gaza.

In the two years after Oct. 7, the U.S. spent at least $21.7 billion in military aid to Israel, according to a paper by William D. Hartung, a senior research fellow at the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, a think tank based in Washington.

title: U.S. military carries out limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island
summary: The strikes, which appeared to be limited as opposed to a full return to hostilities, came on the eve of crucial American midterm elections.
story: The U.S. military carried out limited strikes Monday on Iran’s Qeshm Island, according to two U.S. officials.

The officials said the U.S. attacks, which came on the eve of crucial U.S. midterm elections and as the Middle East is anxious about the possibility of a return to all-out war, were not a resumption of major combat operations in Iran. They described the attacks as self-defense in response to Iran’s ongoing efforts to target maritime shipping and U.S. assets.
The U.S. continues to intercept drones and missiles that are targeting shipping every day, one of the U.S. officials said.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has routinely targeted and shot at U.S. manned and unmanned aircraft over the Strait of Hormuz and in the area over the past few weeks, one of the U.S. officials said.
The U.S. is occasionally striking Iranian missile launchers in self-defense when the Revolutionary Guard shoots at U.S. aircraft, the official said.
Iran tried to target a U.S. aircraft again, leading to the U.S. strike on Qeshm to take out the launcher, the official said, calling it part of ongoing operations.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
A third U.S. official said, “This was a defensive measure for Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against U.S. assets.”
Iranian state media reported that five explosions were heard Monday on Qeshm Island.
President Donald Trump had said the U.S. would not launch strikes on Iran before Tuesday’s midterm elections.

Asked on “Fox & Friends” what would happen once the elections were over, Trump said he wasn’t looking to “kill lots of people,” but “if we have to, we’ll have to.” The latest strikes were “just a minor attack,” he said while insisting the situation does not constitute a war.
The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on U.S. gasoline prices and other parts of the economy have been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress.

The administration was last known to have carried out some attacks in early September, but thousands of U.S. troops remain in the waters off Iran to maintain a naval blockade aimed at preventing tankers carrying Iranian oil from getting to the global market. A third aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are also on their way to the Middle East.

Earlier Monday, Vice President JD Vance offered measured optimism that a deal can still be struck to prevent Trump from following through on his threat to potentially order new strikes on Iran after the midterm elections.

title: Supermarkets across Europe hit by new fridge cyberattacks
summary: The incidents caused temperature spikes and spoiled food at stores in Sweden, the Netherlands, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg and Estonia. It follows a similar cyberattack in France last month.
story: Supermarkets across Europe were hit Monday by a new wave of apparent cyberattacks affecting fridges and freezers.
The incidents caused temperature spikes and spoiled food at stores in Sweden, the Netherlands, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg and Estonia.

They follow a cyberattack in France last month, in which, police said, hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, raising temperatures as high as 122 degrees Fahrenheit and causing fires and food losses.
Authorities have not indicated who could have been behind the incidents. There were no claims of responsibility.
The continent is confronting broader security fears stemming from Russia’s war in Ukraine.
The new cyberattack highlights how digital threats can increasingly affect people’s everyday lives, the European Commission said Monday.

title: Fake alerts warn of nuclear danger as Ukraine and Russia report emergency app hacks
summary: The dueling accusations came just as a rare humanitarian ceasefire between the two sides ended, raising fears of intensified fighting.
story: Nuclear danger, radiation threat and street combat: Ukrainians received a wave of messages Sunday night that raised alarm with a series of grave — and baseless — warnings.

Authorities said the country’s emergency alert application had been targeted in a cyberattack, and hours later Russia said its own alert system had also been hacked. The dueling accusations came just as a rare humanitarian ceasefire between the two sides ended, raising fears of intensified fighting rather than a move toward broader peace.

Residents in Ukraine have become used to the unsettling alerts that buzz their phones with news of incoming Russian missiles and drones — a service millions rely on to seek shelter before the attacks hit their cities. But the warnings Sunday night immediately stood out.
